_comment: Carve-out from 01-auth.json's strict /api/v1/auth/* tier for the QR-login phone side (scan/confirm/deny) only - qr/create and qr/status stay on the strict tier, unchanged, since they're genuinely unauthenticated. scan/confirm/deny are the opposite: an already-logged-in phone approving a ticket (48-char random, single-use, Laravel's own throttle:20,1 / throttle:10,1 already keyed per authenticated user underneath) - not a credential-stuffing target, so they don't need 01-auth.json's 30-req/60s-per-IP budget. That shared budget was the actual bug: login-content.tsx's QR-status poll (every 3s while the website's code is on screen) is documented there as deliberately consuming ~20 of that 30, and the phone doing the scanning is almost always on the SAME IP as the browser being polled (the normal case - phone and laptop on the same WiFi), so the phone's own scan()/confirm() calls got starved by the website's own polling and rejected with a bare gateway 429 that reads as 'Too many attempts' with no other explanation. Priority 11 (> 01-auth.json's 10) so this wins for these three specific paths; everything else under /api/v1/auth/* is unaffected. Rate limit matches 04-authenticated.json's own tier - normal authenticated app usage.
name: teezer-auth-qr-approval
desc: QR-login phone-side approval (scan/confirm/deny) - authenticated-tier rate limit
